content.comment_body: Hello. I have not used the [product_name] controller yet and am evaluating its suitability for a project before purchasing hardware. I need to generate a voltage output (0-10V) that changes in steps over 24–48 hours, with intervals typically 1 hour and using between 6 and 10 distinct voltage levels. For example, the output should start at zero volts and increment at set intervals until the total time passes, then return to zero. I expect to need a basic controller and an analog output extension module. After searching older forum posts, I didn't find examples of clock-driven analog output profiles, and noticed the analog multiplexer may only offer four fixed output values. Is there a way to enable 6-10 output levels? Please confirm whether the [product_name] controller and analog output module can achieve this, and share any implementation examples for [product_name] engineering software. Any assistance would be appreciated.
Welcome to the forum. What you described is possible: you can connect multiple Analog-MUX modules to achieve more output values.

Thank you for your quick reply. I'll proceed to order some hardware. Meanwhile, I have downloaded the demo version of [product_name] engineering software and will review some tutorials. Are there any .lsc examples of cascaded analog multiplexers available? Also, could a clock-driven shift register or a BCD counter generate the selection lines for the mux? Any recommendations or example projects to start with would be great. Thanks again.
I can prepare an example for you.
Here’s another example featuring analog value addition.
Thank you very much. I have now ordered the [product_name] kit, and will review your examples once I learn the basics. I'll keep you updated on my progress.

[user_name], I have started learning [product_name] engineering software and your solutions fit my requirements well. I find the shift register approach easier to understand since I haven’t explored advanced math functions yet. I’ll need to make minor changes, but your input covers the core. I noticed your solution uses a shift register supported only in [product_name] [version_no] and later. What does FS4 refer to, and how can I verify if my 12/24RCE controller will be compatible? I understand earlier shift registers lacked a reset function needed for my application. Thanks again.

Only old controllers from the initial [article_no] generation lacked a reset input for the shift register. That’s why I programmed it for [product_name] [version_no], since you mentioned you are about to purchase your first controller. Currently, only the latest [product_name] [version_no] is available from retailers. Older models are no longer supplied. Edit: An attachment with a brief history of the [article_no] base modules is included.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is exploring whether a [product_name] programmable controller, along with an analog output expansion, can create a stepped analog voltage profile over extended durations with more than four distinct analog levels. The user is unclear about hardware and software constraints and seeks confirmation on solutions. Experienced contributors suggest that cascading analog multiplexers allows extra output levels and provide various example implementations. The user also receives clarification about using shift registers with reset inputs for timing control, supported in newer hardware versions, helping the user ensure compatibility.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to produce a customizable, stepwise analog output profile with a [product_name] controller, requiring more output levels than the standard analog multiplexer offers. They are looking for confirmation regarding the feasibility, hardware version compatibility, and effective programming approaches in [product_name] engineering software.
